destination.title: Cosmic acceleration, gravitational dynamics and consistency tests
destination.question: Which mechanisms, observations and consistency conditions help assess gravitational explanations of cosmic evolution and additional interactions?
destination.summary: A proposed navigation family spanning ordinary gravitational cosmology, precision tests and conditional quantum-gravity applications. Its branches have different targets and assumptions; shared membership does not identify their questions or establish their conclusions.

systems: Cosmological matter, scalar and vacuum components
Classical and proposed modified gravitational theories
Laboratory, Solar System and compact-object gravity
Dark particles and cosmological effective field theories
targets: Acceleration mechanisms and their observational discrimination
Additional forces, screening and varying couplings
Dynamical consistency, singularities and finite-action criteria
regimes: Early and late cosmology, distinguished by source
Higher-dimensional settings only where explicitly supplied
assumptions: Each model retains its own premises; there is no common Swampland assumption.
Numerical proximity and source-object relations do not establish question equivalence.
Ordinary and pre-Swampland investigations remain eligible.
conventions: Frame, normalization, matter coupling and perturbation conventions remain source-specific.
Observational statements retain their supplied source dates and limitations.
includes: Separate overview questions with source-scoped fine identities
Alternate access to scalar-star dynamics and peripheral field-theory questions
excludes: Universal viability or exclusion claims inferred from abstracts
Equating identical background expansion with identical gravitational physics
Treating acoustic propagation or astronomical scaling as established acceleration mechanisms

readingCoverage.readingLimit: Supplied descriptions, bounded primary excerpts and explicitly typed graph context only. No images, full papers, cited calculations or current observational status were independently verified. This authored scope remains a proposal.

sources.title: f(R) theories

evidence.text: Which f(R) theories can produce inflation or late-time acceleration while satisfying cosmological, stability and local-gravity requirements, and which perturbation observables distinguish viable models from GR or ΛCDM?

sources.title: Unified cosmic history in modified gravity: from F(R) theory to Lorentz non-invariant models

evidence.text: Can classical modifications of gravity provide a unified account of early inflation and late cosmic acceleration, reconstruct prescribed expansion histories, and avoid future singularities while satisfying local constraints?

sources.title: Palatini Approach to Modified Gravity: f(R) Theories and Beyond

evidence.text: Review whether gravity with independently varied metric and connection can explain cosmic acceleration, satisfy local and stellar tests, admit a satisfactory initial-value formulation, and describe nonsingular high-density cosmology.

sources.title: Modified Gravity and Cosmology

evidence.text: How can modified gravitational theories differ observably from GR and from one another while satisfying established gravitational tests, and can their cosmology address dark matter, acceleration or the cosmological constant problem?

sources.title: Backreaction in late-time cosmology

evidence.text: Can nonlinear structure formation in classical GR change average expansion, spatial curvature and light propagation enough to explain late-time cosmological observations without dark energy or modified gravity?

sources.title: Dark Matter and Dark Energy Interactions: Theoretical Challenges, Cosmological Implications and Observational Signatures

evidence.text: Can non-gravitational DM–DE interactions alleviate the coincidence problem while preserving viable expansion and structure formation, and which observations can distinguish or constrain them?

sources.title: Modified Gravity Theories on a Nutshell: Inflation, Bounce and Late-time Evolution

evidence.text: How can modified gravity describe inflation, late-time acceleration and cosmological bounces, potentially unifying the two accelerating eras while satisfying observational and local-gravity constraints?

sources.title: Coincident General Relativity

evidence.text: Can GR be formulated using a flat, torsion-free affine geometry with a removable connection and a boundary-term-free gravitational action, and can this formulation provide simple modified-gravity cosmologies?

sources.title: Coupling matter in modified $Q$ gravity

evidence.text: Can nonminimal coupling between nonmetricity and matter provide a second-order alternative to curvature–matter couplings, and what energy exchange, forces and accelerating cosmological backgrounds follow?

sources.title: f(R) and Brans-Dicke Theories and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can modified gravity satisfy conjectural Einstein-frame potential bounds while retaining a GR vacuum, acceptable stability and a cosmological inflation or dark-energy phase?

sources.title: Dark energy beyond quintessence: Constraints from the swampland

evidence.text: Which more general modified-gravity models can explain late-time acceleration while satisfying observational bounds and the assumed swampland conditions?

sources.title: Swampland conjecture in $f(R)$ gravity by the Noether Symmetry Approach

evidence.text: Can nonlinear curvature dynamics supply effective cosmological density and pressure beyond ordinary matter? The reviewed formulation groups f(R) corrections into a curvature fluid in Einstein-like equations.

sources.title: Uplifting of AdS type to quintessence-like potential induced by frozen large-scale Lorentz violation

evidence.text: Could an early Lorentz-violating gravitational regime leave a frozen remnant that affects cosmic expansion after inflation? The hypothesized remnant supplies the physical motivation for a late-time contortion field.

sources.title: Finite Action Principle Revisited

evidence.text: What restrictions on cosmological geometry, matter, singularities, dark energy and modified gravity follow from imposing finite gravitational and matter actions over the universe's entire spacetime?

sources.title: The Effective Potential Originating from Swampland and the Non-trivial Brans-Dicke Coupling

evidence.text: Can a scalar-dependent gravitational coefficient represent contortion density histories that a minimally coupled canonical scalar cannot reproduce?

sources.title: Model independent analysis of supernova data, dark energy, trans-Planckian censorship and the swampland

evidence.text: How can different microscopic sources of cosmic acceleration be compared through a shared expansion history? The paper represents them by effective energy density and pressure in a homogeneous and isotropic Einstein-gravity background.

sources.title: Spatial curvature and large scale Lorentz violation *

evidence.text: Can a large-scale Lorentz-violation cosmology with nonzero spatial curvature reproduce late-time distance and expansion behavior, and what restrictions follow on curvature, bare vacuum energy and cosmological contortion? The historical H0 tension motivates the investigation.

sources.title: Early and late time cosmology: the f(R) gravity perspective

evidence.text: Can Noether-selected f(R) models describe early and late cosmic acceleration through geometry, accommodate a matter-dominated era, and satisfy energy-condition and swampland tests? Could different gravitational regimes help alleviate cosmological tensions?

sources.title: Cotton Gravity: the cosmological constant as spatial curvature

evidence.text: Can the Codazzi formulation of Cotton Gravity produce nontrivial FLRW solutions, and can its additional geometric freedom give a covariant spatial-curvature interpretation of the cosmological constant while retaining a well-posed initial-value description?

sources.title: A model of dark matter–dark energy interaction with some cosmic consequences

evidence.text: Can a phenomenological DM–DE interaction combined with a prescribed cosmic scale factor describe late acceleration and satisfy energy-condition, sound-speed and swampland diagnostics?

sources.title: Swamplandish Unification of the Dark Sector

evidence.text: Can quantum-gravity consistency connect the small positive dark energy to graviton dark matter, explain the cosmological coincidence and “why now” problems, and organize particle-physics hierarchies?

sources.title: Confronting dark energy in Harada's Conformal Killing Gravity with observational data

evidence.text: Can Harada's Conformal Killing Gravity explain late acceleration and alleviate the Hubble tension through its fixed phantom component, either alone or alongside a cosmological constant, when tested against the TCC and the paper's cosmological data combination?

sources.title: Curvature quintessence

evidence.text: Can higher-order curvature terms supply effective negative pressure and accelerated cosmological expansion without introducing a separate minimally coupled quintessence field? Which f(R) choices admit exact examples, and how do their Jordan- and Einstein-frame descriptions connect?

sources.title: Tests of scalar-tensor gravity

evidence.text: Which features of scalar–tensor gravity are constrained by solar-system experiments, compact binaries and cosmology, and when must local and cosmological observations be combined to discriminate between theories?

sources.title: Ghost condensation and a consistent infrared modification of gravity

evidence.text: Can a scalar sector with a timelike derivative condensate provide a calculable infrared modification of gravity, with healthy low-energy excitations even when gravity is decoupled, and what gravitational or matter signals follow?

sources.title: Dynamics of dark energy

evidence.text: What explains late-time cosmic acceleration, and how can observations distinguish a cosmological constant from dynamical dark energy or modified gravity? This is a review of selected approaches.

sources.title: Predictive Power of Strong Coupling in Theories with Large Distance Modified Gravity

evidence.text: What necessary consistency conditions govern cosmological-distance modifications of gravity, and can strong coupling predict source-dependent deviations accessible to shorter-distance gravitational tests?

sources.title: Probing Dynamics of Boson Stars by Fast Radio Bursts and Gravitational Wave Detection

evidence.text: Can additional scalar interactions substantially increase stable boson-star compactness, and can stellar mass and compactness distinguish the interactions through FRB lensing or binary gravitational waves?

sources.title: The Fate of Dense Scalar Stars

evidence.text: How does general-relativistic gravity, together with nonlinear self-interactions, change the fate of dense real scalar stars near the oscillon/oscillaton boundary, including for potentials asymmetric about their minima?

sources.title: Hubble sinks in the low-redshift swampland

evidence.text: How large an interaction is available under external fifth-force constraints? The source quotes a stronger galaxy bound than its CMB bound, then tests a relaxed coupling while fixing the present baryon fraction.

sources.title: f(R) theories

evidence.text: Metric variation and the trace equation 3□F+FR−2f=κ²T identify the scalaron. An auxiliary-field action establishes a scalar-tensor representation; a conformal transformation constructs the Einstein-frame action.

sources.title: Unified cosmic history in modified gravity: from F(R) theory to Lorentz non-invariant models

evidence.text: Inverse reconstruction uses cosmic time or e-folding. Explicitly, without matter, ω(φ)=−2f′(φ)/κ² and V(φ)=[3f(φ)²+f′(φ)]/κ² give φ=t and H=f(t); an analogous construction identifies φ=N.

sources.title: Palatini Approach to Modified Gravity: f(R) Theories and Beyond

evidence.text: Reviews cosmological phase-space and linear-perturbation analyses, exact spherical and modified TOV equations, and a curved-space Dirac-to-Schrödinger reduction followed by time-dependent perturbation theory for hydrogen decay.

sources.title: Modified Gravity and Cosmology

evidence.text: Cosmological scalar perturbations are treated using gauge transformations, Bardeen potentials and Laplace–Beltrami eigenmodes. CMB/ISW and weak lensing connect observations to gravitational potentials and their evolution.

sources.title: Backreaction in late-time cosmology

evidence.text: Decompose dust kinematics into expansion, shear and vorticity, then spatially average the scalar Raychaudhuri, Hamiltonian-constraint and mass-conservation equations. The resulting Buchert equations couple kinematical backreaction to averaged intrinsic curvature.

sources.title: Dark Matter and Dark Energy Interactions: Theoretical Challenges, Cosmological Implications and Observational Signatures

evidence.text: Background attractor analysis, modified Layzer–Irvine energy balance, Raychaudhuri spherical collapse and Press–Schechter halo counting connect coupling to coincidence, virialization and structure abundance.

sources.title: Light Bending in Models with a Generic Scalar Field

evidence.text: Does a generic real scalar coupled directly to photons change solar light deflection or Shapiro delay, and how can light propagation combined with planetary motion constrain its couplings?

sources.title: Dynamical measurements of deviations from Newton’s $1/r^2$ law

evidence.text: Can orbital precession in a microscopic gravitational system improve sensitivity to Yukawa deviations from Newton's inverse-square law while distinguishing them from electrical backgrounds?

sources.title: Mimetic gravity: a review of recent developments and applications to cosmology and astrophysics

evidence.text: How can mimetic gravity geometrically reproduce cosmological dark matter, inflation, late acceleration and galactic rotation curves, and what limits follow from stability and perturbations?

sources.title: The Effective Potential Originating from Swampland and the Non-trivial Brans-Dicke Coupling

evidence.text: Can an assumed homogeneous remnant of Lorentz boost violation supply cosmic dark energy through torsion?

sources.title: Stringent pulsar timing bounds on light scalar couplings to matter

evidence.text: How do conformal and disformal scalar couplings modify binary dynamics, radiation reaction and post-Keplerian timing parameters, and what bounds follow from the pulsar measurements used in this paper?

sources.title: Weak equivalence principle, swampland and $H_0$ tension with fast single radio bursts FRB 180924 and FRB 190523

evidence.text: Localized fast radio bursts provide redshifts and frequency-dependent arrival times. The paper asks how strongly these observations constrain differential gravitational propagation and whether the resulting sensitivity could distinguish selected dark-energy and Hubble-constant models.

sources.title: <math display="inline"><mi>M</mi><mi>I</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>O</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>O</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>E</mi></math> Mission: Final Results of the Test of the Equivalence Principle

evidence.text: Does the universality of free fall hold for titanium- and platinum-alloy test bodies in Earth's gravitational field at approximately 10^−15 precision? The experiment also searches for apparent composition-dependent acceleration from extremely weak new interactions.

sources.title: Machine Learning and cosmographic reconstructions of quintessence and the Swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Can lensing and growth distinguish the gravitational potentials and reveal a departure from their equality in stress-free GR?

sources.title: Swampland bounds on dark sectors

evidence.text: Can quantum-gravity consistency hypotheses restrict dark particles whose masses, interactions, or abundances evade laboratory and cosmological probes? The paper treats present and inflationary de Sitter backgrounds and compares theoretical restrictions with observationally accessible dark-sector parameter spaces.

sources.title: Causal modifications of gravity and their observational bounds

evidence.text: Can a weakly coupled, long-range scalar modify gravity appreciably near neutron stars while maintaining hyperbolicity, subluminality and solar-system compatibility? What bounds follow from binary precession, stellar structure and radiation?

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: How do proposed quantum-gravity constraints interact with inflationary trajectories, dark-energy model building, modified gravity, and other cosmological systems? This passage maps the reviewed applications without providing the calculations needed to assess most of them.

sources.title: Uplifting of AdS type to quintessence-like potential induced by frozen large-scale Lorentz violation

evidence.text: How does the contortion amplitude depend on length scale, recover local Lorentz invariance and affect long-distance propagation of spinning particles? The paper proposes arrival-time comparisons as a future route to measuring these effects.

sources.title: Cosmological consequences of a principle of finite amplitudes

evidence.text: Can relativistic cosmologies have finite past-to-present saddle actions despite divergent curvature or matter density?

sources.title: A gravitino distance conjecture

evidence.text: Does the GDC remain valid with quantum effects, complete de Sitter moduli stabilization, or cosmological conditions on gravitino propagation?

sources.title: Torsion-balance tests of the weak equivalence principle

evidence.text: How precisely do rotating torsion balances test composition-independent free fall, and what do the reviewed Be–Ti and Be–Al results imply for additional scalar/vector forces, antimatter gravity and interactions with galactic dark matter?

sources.title: Chameleon fields: Awaiting surprises for tests of gravity in space

evidence.text: Can a scalar with order-unity matter couplings evade terrestrial gravity tests through environmental screening while producing detectable fifth forces or equivalence-principle violations in space?

sources.title: A Strong Scalar Weak Gravity Conjecture and Some Implications

evidence.text: Can a local condition on every canonical scalar's self-interactions express gravity being the weakest force, including for massive mediators?

sources.title: Scalar Weak Gravity Conjecture in Super Yang-Mills Inflationary Model

evidence.text: Do scalar self-interaction derivatives satisfy the reviewed gravity-comparison inequalities, under the stated canonical-field and mass-identification assumptions?

sources.title: String-Inspired Running Vacuum—The “Vacuumon”—And the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Can an evolving vacuum component drive early inflation and late acceleration while exchanging energy with cosmological matter?

sources.title: Interplay between Swampland and Bayesian Machine Learning in constraining cosmological models

evidence.text: Can inequalities proposed as quantum-gravity consistency conditions supply useful constraints on a cosmological expansion history before observational data enter the analysis, and can those constraints predict subsequent agreement with expansion-rate observations?

sources.title: Hitchhiker's Guide to the Swampland: The Cosmologist's Handbook to the String‐Theoretical Swampland Programme

evidence.text: Which proposed quantum-gravity consistency constraints restrict cosmological EFTs, especially models of inflation, dark energy, dark matter and black holes, and how strong is their supporting evidence?

sources.title: Extended Theories of Gravity

evidence.text: How can extensions of GR address infrared dark-sector problems and ultraviolet quantum-gravity problems while preserving tested gravitational physics and producing discriminating predictions?

sources.title: Multi-scalar theories of gravity with direct matter couplings and their parametrized post-Newtonian parameters

evidence.text: How do direct scalar–matter couplings modify the ten PPN parameters and solar-system probe dynamics, and can such couplings together with curved scalar target space screen cosmologically active scalars?

sources.title: The Confrontation between general relativity and experiment

evidence.text: Review how experiments test GR, distinguish alternative gravitational theories, and constrain new interactions, from equivalence-principle tests through post-Newtonian and compact-object gravity.

sources.title: Dark Energy from Structure: A Status Report

evidence.text: The setting isolates geometrical effects of averaging ordinary gravitating matter. It removes local pressure and rotational support so that positive regional acceleration, if obtained with zero cosmological constant, must come from the averaging terms.

sources.title: Solar system and atomic clock bounds on locally coupled swampland scalars

evidence.text: Which combinations of late-time scalar motion and microscopic couplings do Solar System, equivalence-principle and atomic-clock measurements constrain, and under which assumptions do these constrain de Sitter swampland realizations?

sources.title: Is Gravity the Weakest Force?

evidence.text: Which scalar mediators can compete with gravity at the cosmological horizon? The proposal includes fields with m_varphi less than or of order H and excludes heavier fields from the horizon-force sum, giving a present-day threshold around 10^-33 eV.

sources.title: Towards a realistic setup for a dynamical measurement of deviations from Newton’s $1/r^2$ law: the impact of air viscosity

evidence.text: How does residual-air drag affect a microscopic orbital test of Newton's inverse-square law, and can revised masses, vacuum conditions and position measurements retain useful sensitivity to Yukawa corrections?

sources.title: Supercritical String Cosmology drains the Swampland

evidence.text: Do scalar-mediated interactions and scalar self-interactions remain sufficiently strong relative to gravity? The paper distinguishes a state-mass gradient conjecture from a conjecture involving second through fourth derivatives of a self-interaction potential.

sources.title: Tests of the gravitational inverse square law

evidence.text: Which theoretical possibilities motivate experimentally accessible violations of the gravitational inverse-square law, what do short-range and astronomical experiments constrain, and how could a detected violation be characterized?

sources.title: Finite-time cosmological singularities and the possible fate of the Universe

evidence.text: Which dark-energy and modified-gravity cosmologies admit finite-time singularities, how are these classified, and which proposed mechanisms might prevent or soften them?

sources.title: Diffusion in unimodular gravity: Analytical solutions, late-time acceleration, and cosmological constraints

evidence.text: Can a specified relation between diffusion and matter density avoid higher-order homogeneous cosmological equations, produce late-time acceleration in unimodular gravity, and remain compatible with supernova, Hubble, and laboratory constraints?

sources.title: Uplifting of AdS type to quintessence-like potential induced by frozen large-scale Lorentz violation

evidence.text: How can cosmic effective gravity retain rotational covariance while allowing Lorentz boost violation? The model constrains boost-connection norms with Lagrange multipliers instead of setting every boost connection to zero.

sources.title: Cosmological consequences of a principle of finite amplitudes

evidence.text: Can nongeneric accelerating histories replace excluded Kasner/BKL beginnings in quadratic gravity?

sources.title: A unified geometric description of the Universe: From inflation to late-time acceleration without an inflaton nor a cosmological constant

evidence.text: Can an infinite higher-curvature gravitational theory generate both early inflation and late-time acceleration using geometry, with neither an inflaton nor a cosmological constant?

sources.title: The environment dependent dilaton in the laboratory and the solar system

evidence.text: Can screened dilaton forces produce differential solar acceleration of Earth and Moon or modify the lunar orbit while ordinary Newtonian gravity is treated as the dominant interaction?

sources.title: Fundamental constants: from measurement to the universe, a window on gravitation and cosmology

evidence.text: How can tests of the spacetime stability of dimensionless fundamental parameters constrain departures from General Relativity, reveal matter-coupled degrees of freedom, and probe possible dark matter or dark energy models?

sources.title: The status of varying constants: a review of the physics, searches and implications

evidence.text: How can laboratory and astrophysical tests of dimensionless coupling stability constrain new physics, equivalence-principle violations and dynamical dark energy, through either detections or improved null results?

sources.title: Dark energy, extra dimensions, and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which geometric restrictions let higher-dimensional Einstein equations constrain four-dimensional cosmic acceleration without specifying the microscopic source of dark energy?

sources.title: New Test of the Gravitational $1/r^2$ Law at Separations down to 52 $\mu$m

evidence.text: Does gravity follow the inverse-square law at detector–attractor separations down to 52 µm, and what additional finite-range Yukawa interaction is compatible with the measured harmonic torques?

sources.title: Chameleon cosmology

evidence.text: Can an environmentally dependent scalar mass allow gravitational-strength matter couplings while suppressing terrestrial fifth forces and retaining observable effects in space?

sources.title: Graviton, ghost and instanton condensation on horizon scale of the Universe. Dark energy as a macroscopic effect of quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can coherent horizon-scale graviton–ghost condensates in self-consistent one-loop gravity explain cosmic acceleration and provide a dark-energy model without additional hypothetical fields?

sources.title: On the Cosmological Implications of the String Swampland

evidence.text: Can controlled quantum-gravity constructions realize a sufficiently small positive slope? Can improved equation-of-state, tensor and dark-sector observations sharpen the proposed restrictions or challenge their cosmological implementation?

sources.title: New regions for a chameleon to hide

evidence.text: How does a tiny quartic self-interaction change fifth-force constraints on a nearly massless scalar with weak-equivalence-principle-preserving matter couplings, and which previously excluded Yukawa parameter regions become allowed?

sources.title: Testing nonlocal gravity with Lunar Laser Ranging

evidence.text: Does cosmological time variation of the effective Newton coupling persist at Earth–Moon scales in RR and DW nonlocal gravity? Can nonlinear structures or the proposed DW screening prevent conflict with Lunar Laser Ranging (LLR), and does RT evade this constraint?

sources.title: Testing different approaches to quantum gravity with cosmology: An overview

evidence.text: How can cosmological observations test or constrain the reviewed quantum-gravity approaches, and what theoretical obstacles prevent reliable predictions?

sources.title: f(R) and Brans-Dicke Theories and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which familiar curvature corrections survive the proposed Einstein-frame potential constraints?

sources.title: The web of swampland conjectures and the TCC bound

evidence.text: How can scalar couplings be compared with gravity, and can an analogous constraint govern a scalar's self-interactions? The source reviews two conjectural formulations and distinguishes them from repulsive-force criteria preventing bound states.

sources.title: Symmetron Fields: Screening Long-Range Forces Through Local Symmetry Restoration

evidence.text: Can a scalar mediate a cosmological force of roughly gravitational strength while evading local gravity tests through density-dependent restoration of a symmetry, and what observable signatures follow?

sources.title: Snowmass White Paper: Implications of Quantum Gravity for Particle Physics

evidence.text: Review how quantum-gravity consistency conditions constrain low-energy EFT and might inform strong CP, the weak scale, new gauge interactions and dark energy. The white paper explicitly does not guarantee that gravitational considerations solve these problems.

sources.title: Weak equivalence principle, swampland and $H_0$ tension with fast single radio bursts FRB 180924 and FRB 190523

evidence.text: How much does a WEP timing limit depend on the assumed foreground gravitational field? The paper compares a fixed Milky Way mass, LSS potential fluctuations and a much more massive Laniakea foreground.

sources.title: The Dynamics of Quintessence, The Quintessence of Dynamics

evidence.text: Can measurements of cosmic expansion and structure growth reveal whether acceleration arises from a cosmological constant, an evolving scalar field, or modified gravitational physics?

sources.title: A Strong Scalar Weak Gravity Conjecture and Some Implications

evidence.text: Must every scalar's self-interactions remain stronger than gravity throughout field space?

sources.title: Logarithmic corrected $f(R)$ gravitational model and swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Use curvature corrections to describe inflation and assess whether their parameters can accommodate cosmological information and the paper's proposed quantum-gravity restrictions.

sources.title: Uplifting of AdS type to quintessence-like potential induced by frozen large-scale Lorentz violation

evidence.text: Can negative bare vacuum energy coexist with late-time accelerated expansion when contortion contributes to gravity? The paper asks whether an apparent quintessence potential can emerge from Lorentz violation instead of requiring an elementary canonical scalar.

sources.title: Introduction to modified gravity and gravitational alternative for dark energy

evidence.text: Can modifications of gravity provide late cosmic acceleration, potentially connect it with early inflation, and remain compatible with local gravitational tests? This is a review of candidate mechanisms rather than an established explanation of dark energy.

sources.title: Varying Constants, Gravitation and Cosmology

evidence.text: How can spacetime variation of fundamental constants be tested, related to gravitation and the equivalence principle, and interpreted through dynamical fields and correlated variations? The review also discusses the more speculative question of explaining their numerical values.

sources.title: Consistency of Cubic Galileon Cosmology: Model-Independent Bounds from Background Expansion and Perturbative Analyses

evidence.text: Which derivative-interaction models remain worth testing after gravitational-wave, local-gravity and ISW restrictions? The paper selects a cubic potential-dominated scenario while distinguishing it from constrained tracker histories and noting possible loss of radiative protection.

sources.title: Exploring thermodynamics inconsistencies in unimodular gravity: a comparative study of two energy diffusion functions

evidence.text: Do barotropic and continuous-spontaneous-localization energy-diffusion functions in unimodular cosmology satisfy the authors’ fluid-entropy requirements S > 0, positive entropy production, and negative second time derivative? What restrictions follow for diffusion parameters?

destinations.title: Which f(R) theories can produce inflation or late-time acceleration while satisfying cosmological, stability and local-gravity requirements, and which perturbation observables distinguish viable models from GR or ΛCDM?

Can classical modifications of gravity provide a unified account of early inflation and late cosmic acceleration, reconstruct prescribed expansion histories, and avoid future singularities while satisfying local constraints?

Review whether gravity with independently varied metric and connection can explain cosmic acceleration, satisfy local and stellar tests, admit a satisfactory initial-value formulation, and describe nonsingular high-density cosmology.

How can modified gravitational theories differ observably from GR and from one another while satisfying established gravitational tests, and can their cosmology address dark matter, acceleration or the cosmological constant problem?

Can nonlinear structure formation in classical GR change average expansion, spatial curvature and light propagation enough to explain late-time cosmological observations without dark energy or modified gravity?
Can non-gravitational DM–DE interactions alleviate the coincidence problem while preserving viable expansion and structure formation, and which observations can distinguish or constrain them?

How can modified gravity describe inflation, late-time acceleration and cosmological bounces, potentially unifying the two accelerating eras while satisfying observational and local-gravity constraints?

Can GR be formulated using a flat, torsion-free affine geometry with a removable connection and a boundary-term-free gravitational action, and can this formulation provide simple modified-gravity cosmologies?

Can nonminimal coupling between nonmetricity and matter provide a second-order alternative to curvature–matter couplings, and what energy exchange, forces and accelerating cosmological backgrounds follow?
Can modified gravity satisfy conjectural Einstein-frame potential bounds while retaining a GR vacuum, acceptable stability and a cosmological inflation or dark-energy phase?
Which more general modified-gravity models can explain late-time acceleration while satisfying observational bounds and the assumed swampland conditions?

Can nonlinear curvature dynamics supply effective cosmological density and pressure beyond ordinary matter? The reviewed formulation groups f(R) corrections into a curvature fluid in Einstein-like equations.

Can additional scalar interactions substantially increase stable boson-star compactness, and can stellar mass and compactness distinguish the interactions through FRB lensing or binary gravitational waves?

How does general-relativistic gravity, together with nonlinear self-interactions, change the fate of dense real scalar stars near the oscillon/oscillaton boundary, including for potentials asymmetric about their minima?

Could an early Lorentz-violating gravitational regime leave a frozen remnant that affects cosmic expansion after inflation? The hypothesized remnant supplies the physical motivation for a late-time contortion field.
What restrictions on cosmological geometry, matter, singularities, dark energy and modified gravity follow from imposing finite gravitational and matter actions over the universe's entire spacetime?
Can a scalar-dependent gravitational coefficient represent contortion density histories that a minimally coupled canonical scalar cannot reproduce?

How can different microscopic sources of cosmic acceleration be compared through a shared expansion history? The paper represents them by effective energy density and pressure in a homogeneous and isotropic Einstein-gravity background.

How large an interaction is available under external fifth-force constraints? The source quotes a stronger galaxy bound than its CMB bound, then tests a relaxed coupling while fixing the present baryon fraction.
How do attractive self-interactions and strong gravity change the fate of initially gravity-supported free-field oscillons: black-hole collapse, dispersal, or a metastable oscillating state?

Can a large-scale Lorentz-violation cosmology with nonzero spatial curvature reproduce late-time distance and expansion behavior, and what restrictions follow on curvature, bare vacuum energy and cosmological contortion? The historical H0 tension motivates the investigation.

Can Noether-selected f(R) models describe early and late cosmic acceleration through geometry, accommodate a matter-dominated era, and satisfy energy-condition and swampland tests? Could different gravitational regimes help alleviate cosmological tensions?

Can the Codazzi formulation of Cotton Gravity produce nontrivial FLRW solutions, and can its additional geometric freedom give a covariant spatial-curvature interpretation of the cosmological constant while retaining a well-posed initial-value description?
Can a phenomenological DM–DE interaction combined with a prescribed cosmic scale factor describe late acceleration and satisfy energy-condition, sound-speed and swampland diagnostics?
Can quantum-gravity consistency connect the small positive dark energy to graviton dark matter, explain the cosmological coincidence and “why now” problems, and organize particle-physics hierarchies?

Can Harada's Conformal Killing Gravity explain late acceleration and alleviate the Hubble tension through its fixed phantom component, either alone or alongside a cosmological constant, when tested against the TCC and the paper's cosmological data combination?

Can higher-order curvature terms supply effective negative pressure and accelerated cosmological expansion without introducing a separate minimally coupled quintessence field? Which f(R) choices admit exact examples, and how do their Jordan- and Einstein-frame descriptions connect?

Which features of scalar–tensor gravity are constrained by solar-system experiments, compact binaries and cosmology, and when must local and cosmological observations be combined to discriminate between theories?

Can a scalar sector with a timelike derivative condensate provide a calculable infrared modification of gravity, with healthy low-energy excitations even when gravity is decoupled, and what gravitational or matter signals follow?
What explains late-time cosmic acceleration, and how can observations distinguish a cosmological constant from dynamical dark energy or modified gravity? This is a review of selected approaches.

What necessary consistency conditions govern cosmological-distance modifications of gravity, and can strong coupling predict source-dependent deviations accessible to shorter-distance gravitational tests?

destination.title: Causality, locality and quantum spacetime
destination.question: How do relativistic field theories and gravitational frameworks define, test or modify causal structure, and which operational and geometric restrictions remain applicable?
destination.summary: Propagation tests, locality, quantum spacetime, energy conditions and operational limits form useful connected directions. Several retrieved sources instead address other EFT-consistency targets or supply methodological settings. Their numerical provenance remains intact while their scientific roles differ.

systems: Gravitational EFTs and selected quantum-gravity frameworks
targets: Signal cones, causal observables and global causal consistency
regimes: Source-specific classical, semiclassical and quantum regimes
Controlled low-energy expansions where explicitly stated
Source-specific dimensions, backgrounds and boundary conditions
assumptions: Numerical membership is a proposal, not a physical premise
Causal criteria require their own reference cones, resolution scales and validity conditions
Different systems and methods may share an overview without sharing a fine question
conventions: Low-frequency phase speed, causal signal propagation and delay relative to a chosen reference are distinct diagnostics
Ordinary and pre-Swampland work remains eligible
includes: Linked alternate homes for noncausal EFT questions and field-construction methods
Explicitly retained historical claims and unresolved alternatives
excludes: Automatic membership based solely on quantum-gravity terminology
A universal inference from a negative delay correction or low-energy superluminality to inconsistency
Treating conjecture compatibility as demonstrated UV consistency

sources.title: Loop quantum gravity corrections to gravitational wave dispersion

evidence.text: How do quantum corrections to gravitational and electromagnetic Hamiltonians change their wave speeds, and can those changes preserve a shared causal cone? A second question asks whether tensor stability and constraint closure constrain the evolution of a discrete quantum-geometric state.

sources.title: Light, Links and Causal Sets

evidence.text: What observable effects could reveal Lorentz-invariant spacetime discreteness, what was the causal-set program's status, and can direct transmission along causal links reproduce the continuum field of a moving source?

sources.title: Causality in Nonlocal Gravity

evidence.text: Do selected weakly nonlocal gravitational theories produce a negative Shapiro time delay in weakly coupled high-energy scattering, and can a field-redefinition construction generate matter-coupled theories that pass this causality test?

sources.title: Limits to Computational Acceleration Imposed by Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Can relativistic time dilation, Malament–Hogarth geometries, or exotic memory fields enable hypercomputation, and what quantum effects constrain the achievable runtime and memory compression?

sources.title: Locality, causality and noncommutative geometry

evidence.text: Does noncommutative interaction actually enlarge the causal light cone to a light wedge, and is nonlocality rather than reduced Lorentz symmetry responsible? What becomes of the usual energy conditions and the notion of local observables?

sources.title: Loop quantum gravity corrections to gravitational wave dispersion

evidence.text: Remove sources, neglect cosmological friction, locally hold the background fixed, and use a plane wave in proper time. The positive-frequency branch yields an instantaneous group velocity, provided the effective equation and short-wavelength approximation both apply.

sources.title: Light, Links and Causal Sets

evidence.text: Replace the continuum retarded Green function, supported on the future light cone up to normalization, by a link indicator. The field at a detector element counts linked source elements, multiplied by a charge prefactor; the detector signal sums this field over its active elements.

sources.title: Causality in Nonlocal Gravity

evidence.text: Pure-gravity arguments use on-shell three-point vertices and imported tree-amplitude equivalence. Scalar examples use Fourier integrals evaluated analytically for simple exponential form factors and numerically for the Kuz’min and Tomboulis choices.

sources.title: Limits to Computational Acceleration Imposed by Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Compare proper times along observer and computer trajectories; combine uniform acceleration with Unruh temperature. Higher-dimensional isometric embeddings supply temperatures in selected curved geometries, with explicit warnings that arbitrary embeddings need not work.

sources.title: Locality, causality and noncommutative geometry

evidence.text: For energy conditions, the authors contract proposed stress tensors with future timelike vectors and examine positivity and causal energy flow. Their noncommutative tensors replace the interaction potential by integrals along a path from a reference point to the observation point.

sources.title: Loop quantum gravity corrections to gravitational wave dispersion

evidence.text: Use the Gauss law to fix temporal and transverse gauge, solve the potential Hamilton equation for electric momentum, and substitute into its evolution equation. The resulting classical equation supplies the electromagnetic baseline for the corrected causal comparison.

sources.title: A Primer on Energy Conditions

evidence.text: What theoretical and epistemic status should local and averaged energy conditions have, given their powerful geometric consequences, interpretive difficulties, and physically important violations? How might they constrain alternative spacetime theories?

sources.title: Causality and gravity

evidence.text: What do perturbative quantum-gravity calculations imply for lightcones, causal uncertainty and microcausality, and which effects are universal low-energy phenomena versus features of the quadratic-gravity example?

sources.title: Superluminality and UV completion

evidence.text: Does a consistent UV completion impose positivity constraints on leading irrelevant operators through causality, particularly when a low-energy theory has superluminal phase velocity and gravity may participate in its completion?

sources.title: Field theories on quantum space-times : towards the phenomenology of quantum gravity

evidence.text: How can field theories on noncommutative space-times expose possible quantum-gravity effects through UV/IR mixing, deformed gauge symmetry, causality and local geometric constructions, without requiring a complete theory of quantum gravity?

sources.title: k-Essence, superluminal propagation, causality and emergent geometry

evidence.text: Can a Lorentz-invariant nonlinear scalar theory have background-dependent signal cones without inevitable causal inconsistency? The distinction is between the symmetry of the action and the preferred frame selected by a scalar configuration.

sources.title: Scalar cosmological perturbations from quantum entanglement within Lorentzian quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can isotropic scalar cosmological perturbations emerge from quantum correlations in Lorentzian GFT, with physical clocks and rods coupled consistently to microscopic causal structure, and reproduce GR perturbation dynamics?

sources.title: On Causality and Predictivity

evidence.text: Should causality or absolute predictivity be fundamental principles, and how much conceptual change is required by fakeon quantum gravity's microscopic dependence on future external forces?

sources.title: Superluminal Travel Made Possible (in two dimensions)

evidence.text: Can consistent Poincare-invariant quantum field theories support superluminal or instantaneous signalling in two spacetime dimensions when spatial parity is broken?

sources.title: Notes from Sidney Coleman's Physics 253a: Quantum Field Theory

evidence.text: How can quantum mechanics accommodate relativistic causality and changing particle number, and how can fields, conservation laws and perturbative scattering be constructed systematically?

sources.title: Causality and momentum conservation from relative locality

evidence.text: Does enforcing relative locality in DSR-relativistic theories on κ-momentum space exclude previously proposed causal loops and failures of global momentum conservation? How severe are the corresponding pathologies without this requirement?

sources.title: Causality Violation, Gravitational Shockwaves and UV Completion

evidence.text: Do superluminal propagation and Shapiro time advances in a gravitational low-energy effective action make it unphysical, or can a causal UV completion remove the apparent violation? Photon scattering and a proposed two-shockwave time machine provide the test.

sources.title: Ultimate physical limits to computation

evidence.text: What upper limits do quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, relativity, and gravity place on computation speed, memory, and serial versus parallel operation? The benchmark is an ideal one-kilogram computer occupying one liter.

sources.title: Phenomenological description of quantum gravity inspired modified classical electrodynamics

evidence.text: How can a broad class of quantum-gravity-motivated corrections to classical electrodynamics be described phenomenologically, and what do they imply for electromagnetic propagation, energy transport, birefringence, and cutoff-related causality?

sources.title: Theoretical and Observational Bounds on Dynamical Chern-Simons Gravity as an Effective Field Theory

evidence.text: How strongly do causality, unitarity, and a perturbative fermionic completion constrain dynamical Chern–Simons gravity, particularly its possible effects on late-universe black-hole and neutron-star dynamics?

sources.title: Causal quantum gravity

evidence.text: How can causality and Poincaré covariance construct perturbative quantum gravity on flat spacetime, while operator gauge invariance controls interactions, physical graviton states and physical S-matrix unitarity?

sources.title: Energy conditions in general relativity and quantum field theory

evidence.text: Which pointwise, averaged and quantum energy restrictions have defensible validity, how do equations of motion affect them, and which geometric consequences survive their classical and quantum violations?

sources.title: About apparent superluminal drives in generic gravity theories

evidence.text: Can the Gao–Wald compact-set time-delay conclusion be extended beyond GR and its null energy/generic conditions through a Raychaudhuri-based continuity argument for conjugate points, and what causal applications follow?

sources.title: Acausal exact vacuum solutions in nonlocal gravity

evidence.text: Does quantum superrenormalizability suffice to exclude acausal Gödel-type exact solutions in pure nonlocal gravity, with neither matter nor a cosmological constant?

sources.title: Non-minimal coupling, negative null energy, and effective field theory

evidence.text: Can nonminimal scalar coupling produce exotic spacetime geometries through negative null energy when treated as an EFT with bounded momenta and field values? Which averaged energy bounds survive classically and quantum mechanically?

sources.title: Reality and causality in quantum gravity modified electrodynamics

evidence.text: What restrictions do real electromagnetic fields and causal response impose on quantum-gravity-inspired electrodynamics, its constitutive relations, helicity-dependent refraction indices, and absorption?

sources.title: Quantum gravity and minimum length

evidence.text: Do distinct quantum-gravity arguments suggest a fundamental limit to position and time resolution, and what would such a limit imply for ultraviolet behavior, measurement, causality and classical spacetime?

sources.title: Don’t throw the baby out with the bath water

evidence.text: What classical correspondence requirements should constrain quantum gravity, can a flat-background perturbative S-matrix supply an adequate definition, and might the apparent ultraviolet failure of general relativity instead reflect limitations of conventional perturbation theory?

sources.title: Shockwaves and time delays in Einstein-Maxwell effective field theory

evidence.text: How do four-derivative interactions correct electrically charged shockwaves and photon time delays, and which contributions are required for invariance under metric field redefinitions?

sources.title: Quantum Theory, Noncommutativity and Heuristics

evidence.text: How can Moyal spacetime noncommutativity accommodate spacetime symmetries, and what signatures arise in particle statistics, scattering, cosmological fluctuations and finite-temperature response?

sources.title: Causality in curved spacetimes: The speed of light and gravity

evidence.text: When do superluminal low-energy photon or graviton speeds and negative scattering-delay corrections in curved spacetime imply a resolvable violation of relativistic causality?

sources.title: Causality bounds from charged shockwaves in 5d

evidence.text: What constraints follow from requiring nonnegative photon time delays on five-dimensional charged shockwaves, with and without gravity, and which accessible regimes give the strongest bounds?

sources.title: Gravitational causality and the self-stress of photons

evidence.text: Do leading quantum matter corrections respect asymptotic causality relative to empty Minkowski spacetime, or bulk causality relative to gravitons traversing the same weak gravitational disturbance?

sources.title: Quantum astrometric observables I: time delay in classical and quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can operationally defined clock comparisons furnish explicit diffeomorphism-invariant gravitational observables, probe classical causal structure, and test whether analogous causal inequalities survive quantization?

sources.title: Arrow of Causality and Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: How do quantization conventions select an arrow of causality, and what determines the macroscopic arrow when ordinary and oppositely propagating modes coexist, particularly in higher-derivative gravity?

sources.title: Electric shocks: bounding Einstein-Maxwell theory with time delays on boosted RN backgrounds

evidence.text: What constraints on leading higher-derivative scalar, Maxwell, and Einstein-Maxwell interactions follow from probe time delays on infinitely boosted Coulomb-like or Reissner-Nordström backgrounds, and what causal interpretation survives the gravitational logarithm in four dimensions?
